Sirisha Pyakurel

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)

Loading data

# Data from reddit user austingwalters in this reddit thread: https://www.reddit.com/r/udub/comments/4e6kxl/i_made_a_website_that_shows_grade_distributions/
# Dataset and FOIA info from their dropbox: https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/8lbyazjlt5jmv86jvvs06/AGtgMaWeyZtZuS2fSYLYn_4?dl=0&e=1&rlkey=1sg7t372nhslxogwjl3e9lt9t

uw_grades_original_df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylethayer/Info-201-au-24-datasets/refs/heads/main/UW-Seattle_20110-20161-Course-Grade-Data_2016-04-06.csv", check.names=FALSE)
 
# From Course_Number get program abbreviation (Program_Abv) and number (Course_Number_Num)
# From Term get Term_Season
uw_grades_df <- uw_grades_original_df |> 
  mutate(
    Program_Abv = str_split_i(Course_Number, " ", 1),
    Course_Number_Num = as.integer(str_extract(Course_Number, "\\d+")),
    Term_Season = str_extract(Term, "Autumn|Spring|Summer|Winter")
  )

Overall Grade Distribution Summary

total_courses <- 
  uw_grades_df |> 
  nrow()

average_gpa <- 
  uw_grades_df |> 
  pull(Average_GPA) |> 
  mean(na.rm = TRUE) |> 
  round(digits = 2)

average_students <- 
  uw_grades_df |> 
  pull(Student_Count) |> 
  mean() |> 
  round(digits = 2)

min_course <- 
  uw_grades_df |> 
  pull(Course_Number_Num) |> 
  min()

max_course <- 
  uw_grades_df |> 
  pull(Course_Number_Num) |> 
  max()

Graphs

ggplot(data = uw_grades_df) + 
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(
    x = Average_GPA
  ),
  fill = "lightblue", color = "black", binwidth = 0.1
  ) + 
  labs ( 
    title = "Average GPA Distribution",
    x = "GPA", 
    y = "Frequency"
    )
ggplot(data = uw_grades_df) + 
  geom_point(
    mapping = aes( 
      x = Student_Count, 
      y = Average_GPA
      ),
    color = "lightblue",
  ) + 
  labs( 
    title = "Average GPA vs. Class Size", 
    x = "Number of Students", 
    y = "Average GPA"
    )

Summary

Overall, the UW dataset contains 39242 courses, with the lowest level being 100-level courses and the highest being 750-level courses. On average, the GPA across all courses is 3.41, which is evident in the histogram since it peaks at around 3.4. The average number of students in a class is around 45.38 students, this is somewhat evident in the scatter plot, with a higher concentration of dots under 100 students in a class.

Comparison #1: CSE vs. BIOL Programs

# Load filtered data sets 
cse_uw_filtered <- 
  uw_grades_df |> 
  filter(Program_Abv == "CSE")

biol_uw_filtered <- 
  uw_grades_df |> 
  filter(Program_Abv == "BIOL")

# cse_uw_df summary stats
cse_avg_gpa <- 
  cse_uw_filtered |> 
  pull(Average_GPA) |> 
  mean() |> 
  round(digits = 2)

cse_avg_students <- 
  cse_uw_filtered |> 
  pull(Student_Count) |> 
  mean() |> 
  round(digits = 2)

cse_total <- 
  cse_uw_filtered |> 
  nrow()

cse_most_advanced <- 
  cse_uw_filtered |> 
  pull(Course_Number_Num) |> 
  max()

  pull(Average_GPA) |> 
  mean() |> 
  round(digits = 2)

biol_avg_students <- 
  biol_uw_filtered |> 
  pull(Student_Count) |> 
  mean() |> 
  round(digits = 2)

biol_total <-

CSE Charts

Bar Chart

ggplot(data = cse_uw_filtered) + 
  geom_col(
    mapping = aes(
      x = Course_Number_Num,
      y = Student_Count
    ), 
    fill = "coral", 
    width = 0.8
  ) + 
  labs(
    title = "Level of CSE Class vs. Student Count", 
    x = "Level of Class", 
    y = "Student Count"
  )

Scatter Plot

ggplot(data = cse_uw_filtered) + 
  geom_point(
    mapping = aes( 
      x = Student_Count, 
      y = Average_GPA
      ),
    color = "coral",
  ) + 
  labs( 
    title = "Average GPA vs. Class Size", 
    x = "Number of Students", 
    y = "Average GPA"
    )

BIOL Charts

Bar Chart

ggplot(data = biol_uw_filtered) + 
  geom_col(
    mapping = aes(
      x = Course_Number_Num,
      y = Student_Count
    ), 
    fill = "darkgreen", 
    width = 0.8
  ) + 
  labs(
    title = "Level of BIOL Class vs. Student Count", 
    x = "Level of Class", 
    y = "Student Count"
  )

Scatter Plot

ggplot(data = biol_uw_filtered) + 
  geom_point(
    mapping = aes( 
      x = Student_Count, 
      y = Average_GPA
      ),
    color = "darkgreen",
  ) + 
  labs( 
    title = "Average GPA vs. Class Size", 
    x = "Number of Students", 
    y = "Average GPA"
    )

Summary

Overall, the average GPA of the CSE program is 3.43, which is larger than the Biology program’s 3.15. The opposite is true for class sizes as well, with CSE’s average class size, 77.68, being smaller than Biology’s average class size of 81.78. The CSE program offers 666 total courses, with the most advanced being a 599 level course. In contrast, Biology offers 816 courses, with 536 as the most advanced. The graphs show that most classes in the Biology and CSE programs have 100 or fewer students, and that lower-level classes tend to have more students enrolled.

Comparison #2: 2010-11 vs 2012-13 Academic Years

  uw_grades_df |> 
  filter(Academic_Year == "2010-11")

data_2012 <- 
  uw_grades_df |> 
  filter(Academic_Year == "2012-13")

Bar Chart

2012-13 Charts

Bar Chart

ggplot(data = data_2012) + 
  geom_col(
    mapping = aes(
      x = Course_Number_Num,
      y = Student_Count
    ), 
    fill = "pink", 
    width = 0.8
  ) + 
  labs(
    title = "Level of Class vs. Student Count in 2012-13", 
    x = "Level of Class", 
    y = "Student Count"
  )

Scatter Plot

ggplot(data = data_2012) + 
  geom_point(
    mapping = aes( 
      x = Student_Count, 
      y = Average_GPA
      ),
    color = "pink",
  ) + 
  labs( 
    title = "Average GPA vs. Class Size", 
    x = "Number of Students", 
    y = "Average GPA"
    )

Summary

Overall, the average GPA seem to stay approximately the same from 2010 to 2013, with it being 3.4 in both academic years. The average class sizes increased slightly, with 2010-2011 being 44.1 and 2012-2013 being 45.02. The most advanced class offered was a 700 level for both academic years, but the total courses decreased slightly from 6,961 in 2010-11 to 6,885 in 2012-13. In the graphs, you can see most class sizes are about 200 and less, with a higher concentration on both years’ scatter plots. On the bar graph, it’s clear that lower level classes tend to have higher class sizes in both academic years.
